source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: Rice stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas and related species) has five species/color forms named in the deck occurring in Asia, distinguished largely by wing color/pattern. Larvae bore into the stem near the base or up inside the culm; early-stage feeding kills the central growing shoot, producing 'deadheart' (tiller death before heading), while feeding after panicle initiation kills the developing panicle, producing 'whitehead' (an empty, white panicle standing out above the healthy canopy). Egg masses are laid on the leaf near the leaf sheath, covered in a felt-like layer of hairs, and can hold roughly 100 eggs each. Natural enemy wasps named include Telenomus, Tetrastichus, and Trichogramma species -- Tetrastichus can attack larvae already inside the stem, while Telenomus attacks the egg mass even before the moth finishes laying it. Predators noted include grasshopper-family predators (Conecephalus longipennis) and crickets (Metioche vattaticollis, Anaxipha longipennis) that feed on stem borer eggs, plus ladybird beetles (e.g. Harmonia octomaculata) and ground beetles (Carabid) that feed on newly hatched larvae; spiders prey on the adult moth.
